topStories.headline: Tenderloin Asks: Where Is Downtown's Revival Money?
topStories.dek: As the Downtown Development Corporation channels $60 million into Union Square and the Embarcadero, Tenderloin and Mid-Market stakeholders say their neighborhoods have been left out of the city's recovery.
topStories.body:
On a July afternoon, Kate Robinson, head of the Tenderloin Community Benefit District, led a small group of Downtown Development Corporation representatives down Turk Street, through Turk-Hyde Mini Park, and around Dodge Alley — a tour that marked a first for the DDC, a nonprofit that funnels private money into public projects. Robinson pointed to the decorative gates on Larkin Street, the monthly Live on Larkin street parties, and art walks made possible by crypto billionaire Chris Larsen's $5 million donation to the TLCBD as evidence of what sustained investment can accomplish.

But the DDC tour was also a pointed message. Since launching last year, the corporation has pledged $60 million to revitalize San Francisco's core — and almost all of it is flowing to Union Square, the Embarcadero, the East Cut, and Yerba Buena. Tenderloin and Mid-Market leaders say their neighborhoods, long associated with the city's most visible challenges, remain on the outside of the private investment wave reshaping the rest of downtown.

The exclusion stings. Larsen's $5 million gift — widely credited as the neighborhood's best private investment news in years — is, advocates note, a fraction of what the area needs. With Larkin Street between Golden Gate and Turk already showing improvement and plans in place to activate the Eddy Street entrance to Little Saigon, the community has demonstrated it can absorb and deploy investment. But Robinson and other stakeholders argue that without capital comparable to what other downtown districts are receiving, those gains will stall.

San Francisco has no universally agreed boundary for 'downtown,' and investors disagree on whether the Tenderloin and the blocks west of Union Square fall within it. For now, that ambiguity appears to be working against the neighborhood. The SF Standard, which published a detailed account of the DDC tour on September 7, found that Tenderloin stakeholders are cautiously hopeful the visit signals a shift — but that no new funding commitments have been made.

topStories.headline: Opera Orchestra and Management Still at Impasse as Opening Night Arrives
topStories.dek: Negotiations between SF Opera management and its musicians' union remained deadlocked as of September 9, leaving the fate of tonight's season-opening 'Simon Boccanegra' at the War Memorial uncertain.
topStories.body:
As of September 9 — the most recent reporting available — the San Francisco Opera Orchestra and management had not reached a new collective bargaining agreement, putting tonight's opening-night performance of Verdi's Simon Boccanegra at the War Memorial Opera House in doubt. The orchestra's previous contract expired July 31, and American Federation of Musicians Local 6 has said its members will not perform unless a fair deal is in place.

The core dispute is over pay. Management has proposed what it describes as a five-year framework that would gradually restructure musician compensation while keeping annual earnings at current levels. The musicians reject that framing: in a social media update this week, the orchestra argued that even a nominal freeze amounts to roughly a 20 percent effective cut against five years of local inflation — equivalent, they say, to rolling wages back to 2018 levels.

The standoff has already disrupted the season's biggest fundraiser. Earlier this month, the Opera moved its annual white-tie Opera Ball — originally set for September 12 at City Hall — to November 12. The 2026 event had been planned around an Italian palazzo theme inspired by Simon Boccanegra, with a cocktail reception, dinner, and after-party recognizing philanthropist Dede Wilsey for 20 years as opening-weekend grand sponsor. The season-opening performance itself remains on the schedule, as does the free Opera in the Park concert originally set for September 13 in Golden Gate Park — both contingent on a contract being reached.

The last time a labor dispute actually canceled an SF Opera opening weekend was in 1990. In 2024, a similar standoff was resolved in the moments before curtain. City Hall will light its dome pink and white this Saturday evening in recognition of Opera Opening Night, per the Civic Center's published lighting calendar — a civic gesture that underscores how much the season means to these neighborhoods regardless of what happens backstage.

topStories.headline: Full Board to Vote Tuesday on Controversial $38.9M OpenGov Permit Contract
topStories.dek: The Board of Supervisors will take a final vote September 15 on a five-year extension of Mayor Lurie's permitting software contract, which critics say bypassed competitive bidding and is already running behind.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco Board of Supervisors is expected to vote this Tuesday, September 15, on a contract worth up to $38.9 million to extend OpenGov as the city's permitting software provider through at least 2031. The contract is the centerpiece of Mayor Daniel Lurie's PermitSF initiative, intended to replace the city's notoriously fragmented permitting infrastructure — spread across multiple departments and software systems — with a unified online portal.

The road to Tuesday's vote has been rocky. On September 2, the Budget and Finance Committee unanimously forwarded the item to the full board — but without an endorsement. Supervisors Matt Dorsey, Chyanne Chen, and Danny Sauter said they supported overhauling the permitting system in principle but were not prepared to formally back the specific deal. Supervisor Jackie Fielder has gone further, calling for a hearing on why OpenGov was selected without a competitive bid and asking the Budget and Legislative Analyst to investigate the procurement. A newly created city inspector general is expected to release its own review of the contract this fall.

City workers have added their own concerns. Staff told Mission Local that running both the old permitting system and OpenGov simultaneously — and troubleshooting persistent technical bugs — has added to their workloads rather than reducing them. The portal went live in February 2026 covering only a limited subset of permit types, well short of the citywide rollout the administration envisioned.

The contract has drawn scrutiny for its origins: the Standard previously reported that OpenGov's founders have financial ties to Lurie's former nonprofit, Tipping Point, and that city evaluators rated a competing vendor, Clariti, substantially higher during the selection process. How the full eleven-member board votes Tuesday will determine whether the city is locked into OpenGov for the rest of the decade — or whether the deal is sent back for revision.

events.title: SF Opera Opens 104th Season: 'Simon Boccanegra'
events.location: War Memorial Opera House, 301 Van Ness Ave.
events.description: SF Opera's 104th season opens with Verdi's Simon Boccanegra, conducted by Music Director Eun Sun Kim, with Amartuvshin Enkhbat in the title role — contingent on resolution of the ongoing orchestra contract dispute. Check sfopera.com for performance status updates.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack: Free Lunchtime Concerts & Food Trucks
events.location: Fulton Plaza, 147 Fulton St. (outside SF Main Library), Civic Center
events.description: Now in its third season, this free outdoor concert series brings live local music and a rotating lineup of food trucks to Fulton Plaza every Tuesday and Thursday through October. The September 15 show features Elise Nova, Kevin Fagan, and Mark Joseph.

events.title: Tenderloin Museum: New Episodes of 'The Tenderloin Diaries'
events.location: The Compton's Cafeteria Riot venue, 835 Larkin St.
events.description: Writers Carolyn Terry and Todd Pickering present two new episodes of their comedic ensemble TV serial set in the 1990s Tenderloin, drawn from Terry's three decades of living in and journaling about the neighborhood.

events.title: SF Symphony: Garrick Ohlsson Plays Brahms
events.location: Davies Symphony Hall, 201 Van Ness Ave.
events.description: Conductor David Afkham leads the Symphony in Unsuk Chin's subito con forza and Schumann's Symphony No. 4, with acclaimed pianist Garrick Ohlsson performing Brahms' Piano Concerto No. 1. Inside Music Talks precede both performances.

events.title: SF Symphony Season-Opening Gala with Hilary Hahn
events.location: Davies Symphony Hall, 201 Van Ness Ave.
events.description: The SF Symphony's official 2026–27 season-opening gala features conductor Giancarlo Guerrero and violin soloist Hilary Hahn performing Mendelssohn's Violin Concerto.

events.title: Fantastic Negrito with the SF Symphony
events.location: Davies Symphony Hall, 201 Van Ness Ave.
events.description: Oakland-born, three-time Grammy winner Fantastic Negrito celebrates the 10th anniversary of his breakthrough Tiny Desk Concert with a full symphonic performance conducted by Jonathan Taylor Rush.

moreNews.headline: City Hall Dome Lights Up Pink and White for Opera Opening Night
moreNews.body: City Hall's dome is scheduled to glow pink and white on Saturday, September 12, in recognition of SF Opera's opening night, per the Civic Center's published September 2026 lighting calendar. The monthly schedule, maintained at sfciviccenter.org, marks national days, awareness campaigns, and major cultural events throughout the year.

moreNews.headline: Opera Ball Rescheduled to November 12 at City Hall
moreNews.body: San Francisco Opera has moved its 2026 Opera Ball from September 12 to Thursday, November 12, still at City Hall. The event had been planned around an Italian palazzo theme tied to Simon Boccanegra, with a cocktail reception, dinner, and after-party. The Opera said decoupling the gala from opening night gives both sides in the contract negotiation more room to reach a resolution without uncertainty affecting ticketholders and event producers. The rescheduled Ball will not include a staged opera performance.

restaurants.name: Brenda's French Soul Food
restaurants.description: A beloved Tenderloin institution famed for beignets, shrimp and grits, and a weekday lineup of $5 breakfast sandwiches with New Orleans flair.

restaurants.name: Saigon Sandwich
restaurants.description: A Tenderloin institution since the early 1980s serving fresh, affordable bánh mì that The New York Times Magazine once called the best in the country.

restaurants.name: Outta Sight Pizza
restaurants.description: Popular Tenderloin slice shop serving excellent thin-crust pizza by the slice in an unpretentious neighborhood setting on Larkin Street.

restaurants.name: Mensho Tokyo
restaurants.description: Michelin-recognized ramen bar famed for its Toripaitan and Duck Matcha ramen, drawing devoted lines since opening its first U.S. location in the Tenderloin in 2016.

restaurants.name: Pho 2000
restaurants.description: Casual Little Saigon spot in the Tenderloin serving authentic phở, vermicelli bowls, and Vietnamese classics at very reasonable prices.

restaurants.name: Chao Pescao
restaurants.description: Vibrant Tenderloin spot serving Latin American cuisine including tostones, seafood dishes, and creative cocktails in a lively atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Tadu Ethiopian Kitchen
restaurants.description: Welcoming Tenderloin restaurant serving traditional Ethiopian stews, injera, and generous vegetarian platters in a warm communal setting.

restaurants.name: Wanjai Restaurant & Bar
restaurants.description: Family-run Tenderloin restaurant serving Northern Thai cuisine including khao soi, grilled meats, and house specialty noodles in an inviting atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Ararat Kebab & Gyros
restaurants.description: Tenderloin counter-service spot renowned for its kofte, gyros, and Turkish-style kebabs; a consistent neighborhood favorite.

restaurants.name: Azalina's
restaurants.description: A Tenderloin gem offering beautifully crafted Malaysian street food elevated with California ingredients in a stunning, art-filled dining room.

restaurants.name: Sungho
restaurants.description: A fantastic Korean comfort food spot in the Tenderloin drawing neighborhood regulars and cross-city visitors for warming, hearty dishes.

restaurants.name: Hai Ky Noodles
restaurants.description: A beloved Tenderloin noodle shop in Little Saigon specializing in egg noodles, wonton soup, and strong Vietnamese iced coffee.

restaurants.name: Villon
restaurants.description: All-day restaurant inside the San Francisco Proper Hotel serving seasonal California cuisine in a Kelly Wearstler-designed space with artistic flair.

restaurants.name: Charmaine's
restaurants.description: One of San Francisco's most sought-after rooftop bars, atop the SF Proper Hotel, with panoramic city skyline views, craft cocktails, and a fire pit.
restaurants.address: 45 McAllister St, rooftop, San Francisco, CA 94102

restaurants.name: Bodega SF
restaurants.description: A laid-back Tenderloin bar and kitchen offering hearty comfort food and a well-stocked bar in a relaxed neighborhood setting.

hotels.name: San Francisco Proper Hotel
hotels.description: A 131-room luxury hotel inside a historic 1904 Beaux-Arts flatiron building on Market Street, with Kelly Wearstler interiors, a rooftop bar, and four dining venues.
hotels.address: 45 McAllister St (entrance; 1100 Market St), San Francisco, CA 94102

hotels.name: Phoenix Hotel
hotels.description: Iconic rock-and-roll motor lodge open under new ownership since early 2026, with a courtyard pool, free parking, and nearly 40 years of musical legend.

hotels.name: The Tilden Hotel
hotels.description: A stylish boutique hotel near Union Square and Civic Center with a relaxed atmosphere and a well-regarded breakfast, convenient for arts and theater visits.

hotels.name: Civic Center Motor Inn
hotels.description: A budget-friendly, centrally located motel in Mid-Market within walking distance of Davies Symphony Hall, the War Memorial Opera House, and Civic Center BART.

hotels.name: Motel 6 San Francisco – Civic Center
hotels.description: No-frills economy motel five minutes on foot from the Asian Art Museum and convenient to BART and Muni at Civic Center.

hotels.name: Hotel Epik San Francisco
hotels.description: A four-star hotel with modern amenities and meeting space, situated ten minutes on foot from Civic Center/UN Plaza with easy BART and Muni access.
hotels.address: 55 Cyril Magnin St, San Francisco, CA 94102

shops.name: Heart of the City Farmers Market
shops.description: A year-round outdoor farmers market at United Nations Plaza offering fresh produce, specialty foods, and prepared items from Bay Area growers, held Wednesday and Sunday mornings.
shops.address: United Nations Plaza, Fulton St at Market St, Civic Center

shops.name: Asian Art Museum Store
shops.description: Boutique inside the Asian Art Museum stocking one-of-a-kind objects, jewelry, books, and gifts sourced from across Asia; no paid museum admission required to browse.

shops.name: SF Main Library Wednesday Used Book Sale
shops.description: Every Wednesday, the Larkin Street steps of the SF Main Library host a browseable used book sale spanning all genres; free and open to all.

shops.name: Artisan Gift Gallery at Fulton Plaza
shops.description: An ongoing artisan gift gallery at Fulton Plaza selling handcrafted goods from local makers as part of the Civic Center public space activation program.

shops.name: Onsen SF
shops.description: A Japanese-inspired bathhouse in the Tenderloin offering communal mineral soaking baths, private rooms, and rotating dinner pop-ups in an intimate setting.

artEntertainment.name: Asian Art Museum
artEntertainment.description: One of the largest museums dedicated to Asian art in the Western world, housing more than 18,000 works spanning 6,000 years of history in a landmark Civic Center building.

artEntertainment.name: San Francisco Main Public Library
artEntertainment.description: The seven-story Main Branch of the SF Public Library serves as a vibrant cultural hub at Civic Center, hosting exhibitions, lectures, film screenings, and community events year-round.

artEntertainment.name: War Memorial Opera House
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's grand opera house, home to the San Francisco Opera and San Francisco Ballet, in a landmark Beaux-Arts building at the heart of the Civic Center arts campus.
artEntertainment.address: 301 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94102

artEntertainment.name: Davies Symphony Hall
artEntertainment.description: Home of the San Francisco Symphony since 1980, this landmark Civic Center hall hosts the Symphony's full season plus touring orchestras and special events.
artEntertainment.address: 201 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94102

artEntertainment.name: SFJAZZ Center
artEntertainment.description: The first free-standing building in America built specifically for jazz performance and education, presenting over 300 shows annually at the corner of Franklin and Fell Streets.

artEntertainment.name: Bill Graham Civic Auditorium
artEntertainment.description: An 8,500-capacity landmark arena built in 1915, operated by Another Planet Entertainment and hosting more than 100 concerts and events per year on the Civic Center campus.

artEntertainment.name: The Warfield Theatre
artEntertainment.description: A 2,250-capacity Mid-Market concert hall opened in 1922 as a vaudeville palace, now operated by Goldenvoice and hosting major touring acts year-round.

artEntertainment.name: Great American Music Hall
artEntertainment.description: A storied Tenderloin music hall with ornate Baroque décor, hosting an eclectic mix of rock, jazz, folk, and roots artists throughout the year since 1972.

artEntertainment.name: The Tenderloin Museum
artEntertainment.description: A museum and walking-tour program dedicated to the history, culture, and resilience of the Tenderloin; currently closed for flood repairs while fundraising to reopen and expand.

artEntertainment.name: Rickshaw Stop
artEntertainment.description: A beloved mid-sized venue near Civic Center hosting indie rock, electronic, dance nights, and DJ events in a comfortable two-room space.

gymsRecreation.name: United Nations Plaza Fitness Court
gymsRecreation.description: A free outdoor Fitness Court by the National Fitness Campaign at United Nations Plaza, offering strength-training equipment and free group exercise classes through Rae Studios.

gymsRecreation.name: UN Plaza Skateboarding Area
gymsRecreation.description: A 13,000-square-foot skateboarding zone at United Nations Plaza featuring iconic elements from San Francisco's street skating history, open to all skill levels.

gymsRecreation.name: Civic Center Plaza Free Yoga and Zumba
gymsRecreation.description: Free Zumba and yoga classes held regularly at Civic Center Plaza and United Nations Plaza, part of the Rec and Park and Civic Center Community Benefit District activation program.
gymsRecreation.address: Civic Center Plaza, Van Ness Ave & Grove St, Civic Center

gymsRecreation.name: Fulton Plaza Open Roller Skating
gymsRecreation.description: All-ages open roller skating at Fulton Plaza between the Main Library and the Asian Art Museum; bring your own skates or blades.

gymsRecreation.name: Tenderloin Recreation Center
gymsRecreation.description: A city-run recreation center in the Tenderloin offering gym facilities, youth sports programming, and community classes in one of the neighborhood's few safe recreational spaces.

gymsRecreation.name: Boeddeker Park
gymsRecreation.description: A fully renovated Tenderloin park at Eddy and Jones Streets with a playground, basketball court, and green space serving as one of the neighborhood's primary outdoor gathering spots.

gymsRecreation.name: Onsen SF
gymsRecreation.description: A serene Japanese-inspired bathhouse in the Tenderloin offering communal mineral baths and private soaking rooms.

gymsRecreation.name: SVN West
gymsRecreation.type: Multi-use event venue with recreational programming
gymsRecreation.description: A large Mid-Market event space that periodically hosts a rooftop Sky Rink skating experience and fitness pop-ups alongside concerts and private events.
